requirements.rule: Authenticated MCP discovery preserves the current bearer session's tool names, schemas and annotations; cached catalogs are isolated between grants.

acceptance.given: Two users have different authenticated MCP catalogs.
acceptance.when: The real discovery path lists Alice, Bob and Alice again using one service.
then: Each user sees only their own tool and exact schema/annotations.

requirements.rule: Tool discovery does not grant access: every call uses the caller's server authorization and a server denial is returned as failure.

acceptance.given: A dynamically discovered read tool rejects the caller.
acceptance.when: The Bot calls that tool through its MCP session.
then: The current bearer reaches the server.
The denial is not returned as success or retried.

requirements.rule: Group and channel conversations expose public host commands and no MCP tools, resources or prompts.

acceptance.given: A service has an MCP client and receives group or channel input.
acceptance.when: The service builds the actual callable tool set.
then: Public host command tools remain present.
No campus MCP tool or MCP session is exposed and no MCP request occurs.

requirements.rule: After interruption, a started mutation with unknown outcome remains durably unknown and is never automatically replayed.

acceptance.given: A durable write started under an expired conversation attempt.
acceptance.when: A fresh session tries to recover the operation twice, offline.
then: The durable result stays unknown.
Recovery needs no server connection and cannot cross jobs.

requirements.rule: Destructive MCP writes wait for durable user approval; denial prevents execution and approval resumes the stored operation exactly once.

acceptance.given: A dynamically discovered destructive operation awaits user choice.
acceptance.when: The user approves or denies and a fresh service resumes.
then: No remote write occurs before approval.
The stored result reflects approval, denial or an uncertain server response.
A repeated model call does not repeat the write.

requirements.rule: Explicit room queries and recognized bare room codes select the public map command.

acceptance.given: Supported room identifiers use ordinary, lowercase or fullwidth input.
acceptance.when: The actual command parser resolves the query.
then: The room command and normalized code are selected with public scope.

requirements.rule: A room map request in a shared conversation emits the available public map image without a generated caption.

acceptance.given: A shared group requests 5201 and the server returns a highlighted map.
acceptance.when: The real coordinator persists the outbound response.
then: The outbox contains exactly the map attachment without caption text.
The durable tool result retains the room data and image reference.

requirements.rule: An unavailable room map returns an explanatory message without an image.

acceptance.given: The server reports an unavailable room.
then: The response explains that no map was found.
No image is attached.

requirements.rule: A floor overview uses the available public source image while retaining overview status.

acceptance.given: The server has a floor overview but no highlighted room.
then: The source image is selected.
The structured result preserves overview status without a caption.

requirements.rule: A private MCP room-map result delivers its available image without a synthetic caption.

acceptance.given: The private conversation receives a highlighted catalog_rooms_map result.
acceptance.when: The actual MCP presentation adapter delivers the result.
then: The available image URL is delivered without caption text.

requirements.rule: Unrelated messages and ambiguous multiple bare room codes must not be captured as single-room lookups.

acceptance.given: Messages contain dates, course identifiers, ordinary prose or multiple room codes.
acceptance.when: The command parser examines the message.
then: The message does not become a single-room map command.

requirements.rule: Approval applies only to the persisted intended operation; another target requires its own confirmation.

acceptance.given: The user approved deletion of homework 1.
acceptance.when: The Bot completes it and attempts deletion of homework 2.
then: Only the first target reaches the server.
The second operation durably awaits its own confirmation.

requirements.rule: Ordinary agenda replies display room text without automatically looking up or attaching individual room maps.

acceptance.given: A personal agenda contains a class in 3A101.
acceptance.when: The user requests the agenda rather than a room map.
then: The room remains in the agenda text.
Only calendar data is requested and no room-map image is attached.

requirements.rule: All Bot business HTTP operations use the generated OpenAPI request and matching generated success response model before projecting into command views. Malformed responses fail without partial success. OAuth and MCP protocol transports retain their own protocol clients.

acceptance.given: The checked-in generated operations and every production Life service method, plus a real catalog HTTP server.
acceptance.when: Inspect operation-to-decoder data flow and execute candidate search with valid and malformed typed responses.
then: Every business operation has a matching generated response decoder and no handwritten HTTP request.
Generated filters reach HTTP; valid fields survive projection and malformed field types fail.

requirements.rule: The personal exam command reads every page from the workspace exams endpoint, includes undated exams, and preserves each exam's own semester and course context.

acceptance.given: An HTTP server provides 101 pages with distinct academic records for the authenticated owner, including an undated exam.
acceptance.when: The production Life client reads the full collection.
then: Every page is requested with owner authorization and undated inclusion; dated and undated results retain their own semester and course.

requirements.rule: Failure or invalid pagination on any workspace exam page fails the whole operation without showing a partial list as complete.

acceptance.given: An HTTP server provides two pages with distinct academic records for the authenticated owner.
acceptance.when: The production Life client reads the collection, including invalid later-page responses where specified.
then: Later HTTP errors, invalid field types, repeated page numbers, and unexpectedly empty intermediate pages all fail without partial rows.

requirements.rule: Section homework queries consume the data/pagination collection for the selected section and retain completion eligibility; later page failure does not return a partial list.

acceptance.given: An HTTP server provides two pages with distinct academic records for the authenticated owner.
acceptance.when: The production Life client reads the collection, including invalid later-page responses where specified.
then: Both pages use the selected JW ID and owner token; eligibility survives projection and a later failure returns no partial rows.
